hints: Focus on where an ester bond breaks during acid hydrolysis, it always splits to give a carboxylic acid plus an alcohol.
Look at the left side of the $\text{CO}_2$ group, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}$, this 4-carbon fragment will become the carboxylic acid.
Now check the right side fragment, $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$, add back $\text{OH}$ and name it carefully to distinguish a primary alcohol from a tertiary one.
walkthrough:
**Recall acid hydrolysis of esters**

Think of hydrolysis as adding water across the ester link to reverse esterification. It is like cutting with scissors at the $\text{C-O}$ single bond.

$$\text{RCOOR'} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{H}^+} \text{RCOOH} + \text{R'OH}$$

**Find the acid part from the left**

The acyl part is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}$, which has 4 carbons including the carbonyl carbon. Adding $\text{OH}$ gives $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH} = \text{butanoic acid}$$

**Find the alcohol part from the right**

The alkoxy part is $\text{OCH}_2\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$. Adding $\text{H}$ gives $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$. This is a 3-carbon chain with a methyl branch on carbon 2 and the $\text{OH}$ on carbon 1.

$$\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{OH} = \text{2-methylpropan-1-ol}$$

**Combine to conclude**

Acid hydrolysis therefore gives butanoic acid plus 2-methylpropan-1-ol. That matches the correct pair of names.

options.A: Correct. The left fragment gives the 4-carbon butanoic acid and the right fragment $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$ gives the primary alcohol 2-methylpropan-1-ol. This is the exact split of $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$ with water.
options.B: Incorrect. The acid is right, but 2-methylpropan-2-ol is $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{COH}$, a tertiary alcohol. The ester contains $\text{OCH}_2\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$, so the $\text{OH}$ must be on a $\text{CH}_2$ group, a primary alcohol, not on the branched carbon.
options.C: Incorrect. This swaps the two sides. Students who split the ester on the wrong side of the carbonyl think the branched part becomes the acid. The carbonyl carbon belongs with the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2$ chain, not with the branched chain.
options.D: Incorrect. The alcohol is right, but propanoic acid has only 3 carbons. This comes from miscounting and forgetting to include the carbonyl carbon when counting the acid chain $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{C=O}$.
